angular.pitch: Enterprise Angular apps with clear architecture, for large teams and long-lived products.

0.q: Can you migrate from AngularJS?

vue.pitch: Lightweight, productive Vue.js interfaces, from internal dashboards to online stores.

0.q: Do you migrate Vue 2 apps to Vue 3?
0.a: Yes. Vue 2 no longer receives updates; we migrate with the compatibility build, component by component.

typescript.pitch: End-to-end typed TypeScript, from browser to API, with fewer bugs in production.

0.q: Can you convert a JavaScript project to TypeScript?
0.a: Yes, file by file, starting with the most error-prone modules. Strict mode is enabled in phases.

0.q: Is a React Native app as good as a native one?
0.a: For most products, yes. When a feature needs native code, we write that module in Swift or Kotlin.

flutter.pitch: Flutter apps with a consistent UI on iOS, Android and web, from one codebase.

ios-swift.pitch: Native iOS apps in Swift and SwiftUI, fast, secure and ready for the App Store.

android-kotlin.pitch: Native Android apps in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, stable across thousands of devices.

nodejs.pitch: Node.js APIs and services in TypeScript, fast to build and easy to scale.

python.pitch: Production-ready Python APIs, automation and data platforms.

0.q: Do you also do data engineering with Python?
0.a: Yes: data pipelines with Airflow or dbt, connected to your applications and reports.

java.pitch: Robust Java and Spring Boot systems for sectors where failure is not an option.

0.q: Can you migrate from Java 8 to Java 21?
0.a: Yes, with dependency analysis, regression tests and a phased Spring upgrade.

dotnet.pitch: Modern, maintainable .NET systems, from APIs to enterprise applications on Azure.

0.q: Can you migrate a .NET Framework app to .NET 8?
0.a: Yes, in phases: we map dependencies, cover the essentials with tests and migrate module by module without stopping operations.

php.pitch: Modern PHP and Laravel applications, from commerce platforms to back-offices.

go.pitch: High-performance Go services for APIs, platforms and infrastructure.

aws.pitch: Architecture, migration and operations on AWS, with security and costs under control.

azure.pitch: Architecture, migration and operations on Microsoft Azure, integrated with the Microsoft ecosystem.

google-cloud.pitch: Google Cloud platforms for applications and data, with BigQuery and GKE at the core.

kubernetes.pitch: Secure, well-designed Kubernetes clusters on EKS, AKS, GKE or on-premise.

docker.pitch: Applications in Docker containers, identical from developer laptop to production.

terraform.pitch: Infrastructure as code with Terraform: reproducible, reviewed and auditable environments.

playwright.pitch: Stable, fast Playwright tests that run on every change, across all browsers.

0.q: Why Playwright instead of Selenium?
0.a: More stable, faster and easier-to-maintain tests, with parallel runs and built-in reports. We migrate existing suites by priority.

selenium.pitch: Robust Selenium automation for web apps, in Java, C# or Python, built into your pipeline.

0.q: Our Selenium tests are flaky. Can you fix them?
0.a: Yes. We review waits, selectors and test data, and parallelize with Selenium Grid. Where it makes sense, we move the flakiest suites to Playwright.

cypress.pitch: Cypress tests that are quick to write and debug, for React, Angular and Vue front-ends.

0.q: Cypress or Playwright?
0.a: Cypress is great for front-end teams that want tests that are quick to write and debug. Playwright wins on multiple browsers, tabs and parallel runs. We recommend after looking at the product and the team.

appium.pitch: Automated iOS and Android app tests with Appium, on real devices and emulators.

automation.title: Mobile test automation
automation.pain: Every app release is tested by hand on a handful of phones.
automation.text: Appium suites for iOS and Android that run on dozens of devices on every build.

0.q: Do you test on real devices?
0.a: Yes, on device farms such as BrowserStack or Sauce Labs and on physical devices, with a matrix of models and OS versions based on your app usage data.

jmeter.pitch: Load and stress testing with JMeter and k6 to know what your system can take before your customers do.

automation.title: Load and stress testing
automation.pain: Nobody knows how many users the system can take.
automation.text: Realistic JMeter and k6 scenarios that reveal limits, bottlenecks and headroom.

framework.title: Performance scenarios and data
framework.pain: Load tests do not reflect real usage.
framework.text: Traffic profiles and test data based on production, reusable on every release.

ci.title: Performance in the pipeline
ci.pain: Performance regressions only show up in production.
ci.text: Short k6 or JMeter runs on every release, with thresholds that block the release.

0.q: When should we run load tests?
0.a: Before launches, campaigns and seasonal peaks, and whenever the architecture changes. With k6 or JMeter in the pipeline, performance regressions show up straight away.

postman.pitch: API testing with Postman and REST Assured that catches broken integrations before production.

automation.title: Automated API testing
automation.text: Postman collections and REST Assured suites that validate every endpoint and contract.

0.q: Is Postman enough, or do you need code?
0.a: Postman with Newman covers functional API tests in the pipeline well. For complex scenarios, dynamic data or contract tests, we add REST Assured or Pact.

power-bi.pitch: Fast, trusted Power BI dashboards, connected to your systems and refreshed without manual work.

platform.title: Semantic model and Microsoft Fabric
platform.pain: Every report calculates the numbers its own way.
platform.text: A single Power BI data model, with DAX measures shared across the company.

0.q: Can you connect Power BI to our ERP?
0.a: Yes: SAP, Dynamics, Primavera, PHC, TOTVS and others, through native connectors, the database or APIs, with scheduled refresh and row-level security.

databricks.pitch: A Databricks lakehouse that brings data engineering, analytics and machine learning onto one platform.

0.q: Databricks on Azure, AWS or Google Cloud?
0.a: All three. We pick the cloud where your data and identities already live, to avoid transfer costs and duplicated access control.

spark.pitch: High-volume processing with Apache Spark, batch and streaming, on the cloud you already use.

analytics.title: Analytics at scale
analytics.pain: Queries over historical data take hours.
analytics.text: Spark SQL and optimized formats to analyze years of data in minutes.

0.q: Spark on Databricks or self-managed?
0.a: Databricks speeds up delivery and reduces operations; EMR, Dataproc or Kubernetes make sense when cost or control matter more. We compare both against your real volumes.

airflow.pitch: Pipeline orchestration with Apache Airflow: scheduled loads, clear dependencies and alerts when something fails.

analytics.title: Monitoring and SLAs
analytics.pain: Nobody knows a load failed until the report is wrong.
analytics.text: Alerts, SLAs and automatic retries for every Airflow pipeline.

0.q: Managed or self-hosted Airflow?
0.a: For most companies, a managed service (MWAA, Cloud Composer or Astronomer) is cheaper to run. We deploy on Kubernetes when network or cost requirements call for it.

kafka.pitch: Real-time events with Apache Kafka, to integrate systems and feed data without waiting for the nightly load.

pipelines.title: Integration with Kafka Connect and CDC
pipelines.pain: Systems exchange data through nightly files.
pipelines.text: Connectors and change data capture (CDC) that move data where it is needed, in seconds.

analytics.title: Real-time data
analytics.text: Event processing with Kafka Streams or Flink for real-time alerts and dashboards.

0.q: Managed Kafka (Confluent, MSK) or self-hosted?
0.a: A managed service greatly reduces operations and is our default recommendation. We run self-hosted clusters when latency, network or large-scale cost require it.

postgresql.pitch: Fast, secure, always-on PostgreSQL, on-premise or on managed cloud services.

0.q: Is it worth migrating from Oracle to PostgreSQL?
0.a: Often, yes: it cuts licenses and opens the door to managed services. We first assess PL/SQL code and dependencies to estimate effort and risk.

sql-server.pitch: Well-tuned, protected SQL Server, from transactional databases to reporting.

0.q: Do you migrate SQL Server to Azure SQL?
0.a: Yes, to Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance or SQL Server on a VM, depending on which features you use. We validate performance before the switch.

oracle.pitch: Stable, optimized Oracle Database, with specialists in PL/SQL, performance and migration.

0.q: Do you only administer Oracle, or also write PL/SQL?
0.a: Both: DBAs for performance, Data Guard and backups, and PL/SQL developers for procedures, reports and integrations.

mongodb.pitch: Well-modeled, scalable MongoDB for products with flexible data and heavy traffic.

0.q: MongoDB or a relational database?
0.a: MongoDB works well for flexible data and document reads; complex transactions and reporting often call for PostgreSQL. We assess the data model before recommending.

sap.pitch: Functional and technical SAP consultants for S/4HANA, ABAP and integrations, from migration to support.

0.q: Can you help migrate from SAP ECC to S/4HANA?
0.a: Yes. We assess custom code and data, choose the approach (greenfield, brownfield or selective) and migrate in phases, with regression tests at each step.

salesforce.pitch: Salesforce shaped around your sales and customer service, with Apex, Flows and integrations.

0.q: Do you migrate data from another CRM to Salesforce?
0.a: Yes. We map objects and fields, clean and deduplicate data and migrate in phases, validating before the old system is switched off.

outsystems.pitch: Low-code OutSystems apps delivered fast, without giving up quality, security or integration.

implementation.title: OutSystems apps from scratch
implementation.text: Web and mobile apps in OutSystems, from prototype to production in weeks.

0.q: Do you migrate apps from OutSystems 11 to ODC?
0.a: Yes. We assess architecture and dependencies, prepare the apps and migrate in phases to OutSystems Developer Cloud.

openai.pitch: Assistants, document search and automation with OpenAI GPT models, connected to your systems with your data protected.

0.q: OpenAI directly or Azure OpenAI?
0.a: Azure OpenAI when you are already on Microsoft and need an EU region and network control; the OpenAI API when faster access to new models matters more.

claude.pitch: Applications built on Anthropic Claude models for long documents, agents and automation, with clear safety rules.

0.q: Claude through Anthropic, AWS or Google Cloud?
0.a: Through the cloud where you already have contracts and data (Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI), or the Anthropic API when you want the newest features first.

langchain.pitch: AI agents and applications with LangChain and LangGraph, connected to your data and tools and ready for production.

hugging-face.pitch: Open-source Hugging Face models fine-tuned and hosted on your infrastructure, when data cannot leave the company.

0.q: Are open-source models a real alternative?
0.a: For many tasks, yes: classification, extraction and internal assistants. We compare quality and cost against commercial models before recommending.

pytorch.pitch: PyTorch machine learning models, from experimentation to production, for forecasting, computer vision and language.

assistants.title: Predictive models
assistants.pain: Forecasts are still made in spreadsheets.
assistants.text: Models trained on your data to forecast demand, risk or customer churn.

rag.title: Computer vision and language
rag.pain: Images and text are analyzed by hand.
rag.text: PyTorch vision and language models to classify, extract and detect.
